title: Solana stablecoin holders hit 14M as SOL falls 13% – Can adoption drive SOL?
summary: Solana’s growing stablecoin base has yet to translate into stronger trading activity, network fees, or sustained demand for SOL.
content: Solana has reached 14 million stablecoin holders, marking significant network growth. However, this rising adoption has not yet translated into stronger trading activity, higher network fees, or sustained demand for the native token, SOL, which recently fell by 13 percent.
content_ta: Solana-வில் stablecoin வைத்திருப்பவர்களின் எண்ணிக்கை 14 மில்லியனை எட்டியுள்ளது. இருப்பினும், இந்த அதிகரித்த பயன்பாடு இன்னும் வலுவான வர்த்தக நடவடிக்கைக்கோ, அதிக நெட்வொர்க் கட்டணங்களுக்கோ அல்லது 13 சதவீதம் சரிந்த SOL டோக்கனுக்கான தொடர்ச்சியான தேவைக்கோ வழிவகுக்கவில்லை.

title: Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint says it’s not rushing retail stablecoin
summary: The Standard Chartered and Animoca Brands joint venture previously targeted retail access as early as the end of 2026, but its CEO declined to reaffirm that timeline.
content: Standard Chartered-led venture Anchorpoint has stated it is not rushing to launch a retail stablecoin. While the joint venture with Animoca Brands previously aimed for retail access by the end of 2026, the CEO recently declined to reaffirm this timeline, indicating a more cautious approach to its upcoming digital asset rollout.
content_ta: Standard Chartered மற்றும் Animoca Brands நிறுவனங்களின் கூட்டு முயற்சியான Anchorpoint, சில்லறை வணிக stablecoin வெளியீட்டை அவசரப்படுத்தவில்லை என்று தெரிவித்துள்ளது. 2026 இறுதிக்குள் சில்லறை பயனர்களுக்கு இதனை வழங்க திட்டமிடப்பட்டிருந்த போதிலும், இந்த காலக்கெடுவை தலைமை நிர்வாக அதிகாரி உறுதிப்படுத்த மறுத்துவிட்டார்.

title: Quant Salaries Continue Climbing as AI Reshapes Rather Than Replaces Roles
summary: Compensation for quantitative finance professionals has kept rising even as artificial intelligence becomes more deeply embedded in the industry, according to recent research from the CQF Institute, part of Fitch Learning. The recent research findings, drawn from the organization’s 2026 Careers Guide to Quantitative Finance,... Read More
content: Compensation for quantitative finance professionals continues to rise despite the growing adoption of artificial intelligence in the industry. According to recent research from the CQF Institute, part of Fitch Learning, AI is currently reshaping rather than replacing these specialized roles. The findings highlight sustained demand and strong earning potential for professionals skilled in both quantitative methods and modern technological advancements within the financial sector.
content_ta: நிதித்துறையில் செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு (AI) பரவலாகப் பயன்படுத்தப்பட்டு வந்தாலும், quantitative finance நிபுணர்களின் சம்பளம் தொடர்ந்து உயர்ந்து வருகிறது. Fitch Learning நிறுவனத்தின் ஒரு பகுதியான CQF Institute நடத்திய சமீபத்திய ஆராய்ச்சியின்படி, AI ஆனது இந்த சிறப்புப் பணிகளை மாற்றுவதற்குப் பதிலாக, அவற்றை மறுவடிவமைத்து வருகிறது. நிதித் துறையில் quantitative முறைகள் மற்றும் நவீன தொழில்நுட்பங்களில் திறமையான நிபுணர்களுக்கான தொடர்ச்சியான தேவையையும் வலுவான வருவாய் வாய்ப்பையும் இந்த முடிவுகள் காட்டுகின்றன.

title: Internet Computer tops Solana at 2323 TPS: Why is ICP still falling?
summary: Internet Computer is processing more activity. What would turn that activity into stronger demand for ICP?
content: Internet Computer has surpassed Solana by reaching 2323 transactions per second, showing significant network activity. Despite this high throughput and increased engagement on the platform, the ICP token price continues to fall. Analysts and observers are questioning what factors are required to translate this growing network activity into stronger market demand and a positive price trend for ICP.
content_ta: இண்டர்நெட் கம்ப்யூட்டர் வினாடிக்கு 2323 பரிவர்த்தனைகளை எட்டி Solana-வை முந்தியுள்ளது, இது குறிப்பிடத்தக்க நெட்வொர்க் செயல்பாட்டைக் காட்டுகிறது. இந்த அதிக வேகம் மற்றும் பிளாட்ஃபார்மில் ஈடுபாடு அதிகரித்த போதிலும், ICP டோக்கன் விலை தொடர்ந்து சரிந்து வருகிறது. இந்த வளர்ந்து வரும் நெட்வொர்க் செயல்பாட்டை வலுவான சந்தை தேவையாகவும் ICP-க்கான நேர்மறையான விலை போக்காகவும் மாற்ற என்ன காரணிகள் தேவை என்று ஆய்வாளர்கள் கேள்வி எழுப்பி வருகின்றனர்.

title: Scientists Reversed 60 Years of Cellular Aging. Can It Work in Humans?
summary:
Bonn scientists made 80-year-old cells 60 years younger in a lab. See why it isn't a cure and who funds human trials.
The post Scientists Reversed 60 Years of Cellular Aging. Can It Work in Humans? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Scientists in Bonn have successfully reversed sixty years of cellular aging in eighty-year-old cells within a laboratory setting. While this breakthrough marks a significant scientific milestone, researchers emphasize that it is not yet a cure. Preparations and funding are currently underway to determine if this promising rejuvenation process can eventually be adapted to work safely and effectively in humans.
content_ta: Bonn-ஐச் சேர்ந்த விஞ்ஞானிகள் ஆய்வகத்தில் 80 வயதுடைய செல்களை 60 ஆண்டுகள் இளமையாக மாற்றியுள்ளனர். இந்த சாதனை ஒரு முக்கிய அறிவியல் மைல்கல்லாக இருந்தாலும், இது இன்னும் ஒரு முழுமையான தீர்வு அல்ல என்று ஆராய்ச்சியாளர்கள் வலியுறுத்துகின்றனர். இந்த rejuvenations முறை மனிதர்களிடம் பாதுகாப்பாக வேலை செய்யுமா என்பதை அறிய தற்போது நிதி மற்றும் சோதனைகள் நடந்து வருகின்றன.

title: 3 Big Tech Earnings Reports to Watch as AI Bills Keep Growing
summary:
Big tech earnings arrive this week, with Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon all releasing quarterly reports. In their latest quarters, Google Cloud grew 82%, Azure 42%, and Amazon Web Services (AWS) 37%, while all three spent heavily on AI infrastructure. Microsoft and Alphabet report on Wednesday, hours after the Federal Reserve announces its rate decision at
The post 3 Big Tech Earnings Reports to Watch as AI Bills Keep Growing appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Big tech earnings reports from Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon are set to be released this week. These quarterly updates come as all three companies continue to spend heavily on artificial intelligence infrastructure following strong previous growth in their cloud computing divisions. Microsoft and Alphabet are scheduled to report on Wednesday, coinciding with the Federal Reserve's latest interest rate decision.
content_ta: Microsoft, Alphabet மற்றும் Amazon நிறுவனங்களின் காலாண்டு வருவாய் அறிக்கைகள் இந்த வாரம் வெளியடப்பட உள்ளன. கிளவுட் கம்ப்யூட்டிங் பிரிவுகளில் முந்தைய வளர்ச்சிக்குப் பிறகு, இந்த மூன்று நிறுவனங்களும் AI உள்கட்டமைப்புக்காக அதிகளவில் செலவிட்டு வரும் காலகட்டத்தில் இந்த அறிக்கைகள் வருகின்றன. பெடரல் ரிசர்வ் வட்டி விகித முடிவை அறிவிக்கும் அதே நாளில், புதன்கிழமை அன்று Microsoft மற்றும் Alphabet நிறுவனங்கள் தங்கள் அறிக்கைகளை வெளியிடுகின்றன.

title: L2 Capital Picks Newton to Tokenize $500m Pre-IPO AI Shares
summary:
The Hong Kong investment firm will use Newton Labs' compliance protocol to put late-stage private technology holdings onchain for eligible investors.
The post L2 Capital Picks Newton to Tokenize $500m Pre-IPO AI Shares appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: Hong Kong investment firm L2 Capital has selected Newton Labs to tokenize five hundred million dollars worth of pre-IPO artificial intelligence shares. The firm will utilize Newton Labs' compliance protocol to bring late-stage private technology holdings onchain, making them accessible to eligible investors.
content_ta: ஹாங்காங்கைச் சேர்ந்த முதலீட்டு நிறுவனமான L2 Capital, pre-IPO AI பங்குகளில் ஐநூறு மில்லியன் டாலர் மதிப்பை டோக்கனைஸ் செய்ய Newton Labs நிறுவனத்தைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்துள்ளது. தகுதியான முதலீட்டாளர்களுக்கு பிந்தைய கட்ட தனியார் தொழில்நுட்ப பங்குகளை ஆன்லைனில் கொண்டுவர Newton Labs இன் இணக்க நெறிமுறையை இந்நிறுவனம் பயன்படுத்தும்.

title: India's largest crypto exchange absorbs $16 million loss from internal process failure tied to retired wallet
summary: The Mumbai-based exchange initially dismissed reports of suspicious outflows as a false alarm. It now says it lost $16 million and will absorb the loss.
content: India's largest cryptocurrency exchange suffered a $16 million loss due to an internal process failure involving a retired digital wallet. The Mumbai-based platform initially dismissed reports of suspicious outflows as a false alarm before confirming the financial hit. The exchange has stated that it will fully absorb the loss itself, ensuring customer funds remain unaffected by the security and operational incident.
content_ta: India-வின் மிகப்பெரிய cryptocurrency exchange, ஓய்வுபெற்ற digital wallet-டன் தொடர்புடைய internal process failure காரணமாக $16 million இழப்பைச் சந்தித்துள்ளது. Mumbai-ஐ தலைமையிடமாகக் கொண்ட இந்த நிறுவனம், சந்தேகத்திற்கிடமான பண பரிமாற்றங்கள் குறித்த தகவல்களை ஆரம்பத்தில் வதந்தி என்று மறுத்த நிலையில், தற்போது இழப்பை உறுதிப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த நிதி இழப்பை நிறுவனமே முழுமையாக ஏற்றுக்கொள்வதாகவும், வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் நிதியைப் பாதிக்காது என்றும் தெரிவித்துள்ளது.

title: Bitcoin wallet bug let rogue servers steal funds when users tried to speed up payments
summary: Attackers replaced legitimate transactions with fake ones, then waited for users to approve higher fees. At least one person lost bitcoin before developers patched the flaw.
content: A software bug in Bitcoin wallets allowed rogue servers to steal funds when users attempted to speed up pending transactions. Attackers replaced legitimate payments with fraudulent ones and waited for victims to approve higher fees. At least one user lost funds before developers deployed a patch to fix the vulnerability.
content_ta: Bitcoin வாலட்களில் இருந்த ஒரு மென்பொருள் கோளாறு காரணமாக, பயனர்கள் கட்டணங்களை துரிதப்படுத்த முயன்றபோது போலி சர்வர்கள் மூலம் நிதி திருடப்பட்டது. தாக்குதல் நடத்துநர்கள் முறையான பரிவர்த்தனைகளை போலி பரிவர்த்தனைகளைக் கொண்டு மாற்றி, பயனர்கள் அதிக கட்டணங்களை அங்கீகரிக்கும் வரை காத்திருந்தனர். இந்த பாதிப்புக்கு டெவலப்பர்கள் பேட்ச் வழங்குவதற்கு முன்பு குறைந்தது ஒரு பயனராவது தனது Bitcoin-ஐ இழந்தார்.

title: Bitcoin slips under $80,000 as traders de-risk ahead of Fed meeting
summary: Ether and XRP led losses among the majors as the AI trade took another hit in Asia, where Goldman Sachs cut its Kospi target by 25%.
content: Bitcoin slipped below $80,000 as traders reduced risk ahead of an upcoming Federal Reserve meeting. The market downturn affected other major cryptocurrencies like Ether and XRP. Additionally, the broader sentiment was weighed down by developments in Asia, where Goldman Sachs significantly reduced its Kospi market target, impacting technology and AI-related trades.
content_ta: வரவிருக்கும் Fed கூட்டத்திற்கு முன்னதாக வர்த்தகர்கள் முதலீட்டு அபாயங்களைக் குறைத்ததால் Bitcoin விலை $80,000-க்கு கீழே சரிந்தது. Ether மற்றும் XRP உள்ளிட்ட இதர முக்கிய கிரிப்டோகரன்சிகளும் சரிவைச் சந்தித்தன. மேலும், Goldman Sachs நிறுவனம் Kospi குறியீட்டு இலக்கை கணிசமாகக் குறைத்ததன் மூலம் ஆசிய சந்தைகளில் தொழில்நுட்பம் மற்றும் AI தொடர்பான வர்த்தகங்கள் பாதிக்கப்பட்டன.

title: Elon Musk issues a warning for 'AI neoclouds' as SpaceX borrows $40 billion for chips
summary: SpaceX has raised $40 billion in debt to buy GPUs, while Musk predicts a major shakeout among smaller AI cloud providers.
content: SpaceX has secured $40 billion in debt to purchase advanced computer chips for artificial intelligence applications. Meanwhile, Elon Musk has issued a warning regarding potential market challenges for smaller AI cloud providers, suggesting a major shakeout could be on the horizon as large-scale infrastructure investments continue to accelerate across the tech industry.
content_ta: செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு பயன்பாடுகளுக்கான சிப்களை வாங்குவதற்காக SpaceX நிறுவனம் 40 பில்லியன் டாலர் கடன் பெற்றுள்ளது. இதற்கிடையில், சிறிய அளவிலான AI கிளவுட் வழங்குநர்களுக்கு எதிர்காலத்தில் சந்தை சவால்கள் வரக்கூடும் என்று Elon Musk எச்சரித்துள்ளார்.

title: Musk warns over 200 AI neoclouds face ‘guppy-level death’
summary: The warning comes as Gartner forecasts that more than 80% of specialist cloud providers will cease operating independently by 2030.
content: Elon Musk has issued a warning that numerous artificial intelligence neoclouds face imminent failure. This follows a forecast by Gartner predicting that a vast majority of specialist cloud providers will stop operating independently by the year 2030, highlighting mounting pressure within the sector.
content_ta: செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவுத் துறையில் செயல்படும் பல neoclards நிறுவனங்கள் விரைவில் வீழ்ச்சியைச் சந்திக்க நேரிடும் என்று Elon Musk எச்சரித்துள்ளார். 2030-ஆம் ஆண்டுக்குள் பெரும்பாலான சிறப்பு கிளவுட் சேவை வழங்குநர்கள் தனித்து இயங்குவதை நிறுத்திவிடுவார்கள் என Gartner கணித்துள்ள நிலையில் இந்த எச்சரிக்கை வந்துள்ளது.

title: Hong Kong names Nasdaq-listed Solana Company a strategic enterprise
summary: The Nasdaq-listed firm said it plans to establish Solana validator operations in Hong Kong.
content: Hong Kong has designated a Nasdaq-listed Solana company as a strategic enterprise to boost local technological development. Following the announcement, the firm revealed plans to establish Solana validator operations within the region, contributing to the growing digital asset ecosystem.
content_ta: உள்ளூர் தொழில்நுட்ப வளர்ச்சியை மேம்படுத்தும் நோக்கில், Nasdaq-ல் பட்டியலிடப்பட்ட ஒரு Solana நிறுவனத்தை ஹாங்காங் தனது மூலோபாய நிறுவனமாக அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த அறிவிப்பைத் தொடர்ந்து, அந்த நிறுவனம் ஹாங்காங்கில் Solana வேலிடேட்டர் செயல்பாடுகளை நிறுவ திட்டமிட்டுள்ளதாக தெரிவித்துள்ளது.

title: Canada proposes direct stablecoin cash-outs for small holders with a 1% fee cap
summary:
Covered holders could redeem without a minimum amount, while reserve-market illiquidity could limit daily exits and banking access would still matter.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox

title: Paymentology Powers Mukuru’s Move From Remittances to Everyday Banking in South Africa
summary:
Paymentology, the leading global issuer-processor, is expanding its partnership with Mukuru as the African fintech takes its next step beyond remittances with the launch of the new Mukuru Account & Card in South Africa.
The launch marks an important evolution for Mukuru, bringing everyday financial services together with the cross-border money movement capabilities that have been at the heart of its business for more than two decades.
Supported by Paymentology’s issuing and processing platform, the new Mastercard-enabled proposition is offered in partnership with Bank Zero as the licensed sponsor bank. Through the Mukuru Account & Card, customers can receive salaries and other EFT payments, make payments to South African bank accounts, shop online and in-store, withdraw cash and continue to send money across borders, bringing more of their everyday financial needs into a single proposition.
The launch builds on a longstanding relationship between Paymentology and Mukuru. Paymentology has previously supported Mukuru’s prepaid card programme in South Africa, helping the fintech extend digital financial services to customers who have traditionally relied heavily on cash.
The latest development significantly expands what customers can do. Around 500,000 Mukuru customers already hold a prepaid card, creating an established customer base from which the new Account & Card can grow. Existing customers can now move onto the new proposition, which provides broader functionality and increased monthly spending limits, EFT’s and immediate payments to South African Banks.
For Paymentology, the launch also demonstrates the opportunity created through its partnership with Bank Zero. Paymentology became Bank Zero’s first alliance partner earlier this year, combining Bank Zero’s digital banking capabilities and local market expertise with Paymentology’s card issuing and processing technology. Together, the model enables businesses such as Mukuru to bring tailored financial propositions to market without having to build the underlying banking and payments capabilities themselves.
Kesheni Moodley, Regional Director for Africa at Paymentology, said: “Working with Mukuru over the years has given us a front-row seat to its evolution and the impact it has had on how people across Africa access and move their money. This latest launch is particularly exciting because it brings together two important parts of people’s financial lives: how they manage money day to day and how they support family and communities across borders.
“Our role is to give partners the technology and flexibility to turn ideas into products that work at scale. By bringing together Mukuru’s deep understanding of its customers, Bank Zero’s banking capabilities and Paymentology’s processing expertise, we are helping to connect everyday payments with the cross-border services Mukuru’s customers already rely on.”
Andy Jury, CEO of Mukuru added: “The Mukuru Account & Card represents an important next step in our journey. Our customers have trusted us for more than 20 years to help them move money across borders, and we now have the opportunity to support much more of their everyday financial lives.
“Paymentology has been a longstanding partner to Mukuru and understands both our business and the customers we serve. As we expand our proposition, having partners that can support the scale, flexibility and experience we want to deliver is incredibly important.”
Mukuru has built an extensive physical and digital network across Africa, with more than 320,000 locations offering its services or cash-in and cash-out capabilities. The combination of physical access and digital services allows customers to move between cash and digital finance according to their individual needs.

title: Pepper Money Increases Concessionary Purchase LTV to 85%
summary:
Pepper Money has increased the maximum loan-to-value (LTV) available on concessionary purchases from 75% to 85% of the property’s full market value, giving eligible customers greater flexibility when buying a property at a discounted price from a close family member, or buying the home they currently rent from their landlord. 
 
The change reduces the seller discount needed for eligible purchases from 25% to 15%, where the buyer borrows the full discounted purchase price. Under a concessionary purchase, the difference between the property’s full market value and the discounted purchase price can act as the buyer’s deposit. Eligible customers can borrow up to 100% of the discounted purchase price, including fees, subject to a maximum of 85% of the property’s full market value and applicable lending criteria. 
 
For example, where an eligible buyer borrows the full discounted purchase price without contributing a cash deposit, assuming fees are paid separately, a property with a £300,000 market value would require a seller discount of £45,000 (15%) at 85% LTV, compared with £75,000 (25%) at the previous 75% maximum. The maximum loan in that example rises from £225,000 to £255,000, subject to affordability and lending criteria. 
 
The change could help existing tenants buy from their landlord, or relatives buy from a close family member. 
Paul Adams, Director of Sales at Pepper Money, said: “A close family member or landlord may be willing to sell at a discount, but a 25% reduction can be a significant concession. Increasing our maximum LTV to 85% means eligible buyers borrowing the full discounted purchase price can proceed with a smaller concession from the seller. 
 
“For brokers, it provides another option when helping customers whose circumstances do not fit a conventional purchase.” 
The new 85% LTV maximum is available now, subject to Pepper Money’s usual affordability, credit and lending requirements.

title: Payment Gateway vs. Payment Processor vs. Acquirer: Where Each Layer Ends
summary:
Ask three payment teams where a gateway ends and a processor begins, and you will probably get three different answers. The industry's own reference points don't settle it: the PCI Security Standards Council glossary lists ‘payment gateway' and 'PSP' as alternative names for a payment processor.
For a merchant with one provider and one market, the blur is harmless. At scale, it gets expensive. The payment gateway vs payment processor question is really a question of ownership: who holds the card data, who talks to the card schemes, who moves the money, and who pays when something goes wrong. Each answer points to a different contract, a different cost line, and a different switching cost.
Here is how we draw those lines at Corefy, where we connect merchants and payment institutions to providers across many markets, and where orchestration fits once the lines are clear.
The ownership test: what each layer actually controls
The fastest way to place any provider in your stack is to ask what it owns and who it answers to.
 





Layer
What it owns
Who it answers to
What it does not do
Payment gateway
Secure capture and transmission of payment data from the checkout
The merchant; PCI DSS as a service provider
Move funds or carry credit risk
Payment processor
Authorization and clearing messages to and from the card schemes
The acquirer, which registers it with the schemes
Sign merchants or settle funds in its own name
Acquiring bank
The merchant agreement, settlement, and financial liability
The card schemes and their financial regulator
Decide what happens to a transaction before it arrives
Payment orchestrator
Routing logic, data normalization, and reporting across providers
The merchant
Hold an acquiring license or absorb chargeback liability
 
In practice, these layers rarely arrive separately. A typical PSP contract bundles gateway, processing, and acquiring into one integration, one contract, and one invoice. That is a sensible way to start. The cost shows up later, when you want to change one layer and discover the other two come with it.

Payment gateway vs payment processor: two jobs that usually share a contract
The gateway is the merchant-facing end. It receives card data from a checkout page, app, or terminal, encrypts and forwards it. Because it handles cardholder data on someone else's behalf, PCI DSS treats it as a service provider, with the heavier compliance obligations that status carries. A gateway does not move money. You can replace it without touching your settlement arrangements, which makes it the cheapest layer to change.
The processor sits one step deeper. It converts the transaction into the message formats the card schemes expect, sends authorization requests, and handles clearing at the end of the day. Its client is usually the acquirer. Visa requires acquirers to register every third-party agent that performs services on their behalf, and the acquirer answers for them.

 
That relationship defines the processor's risk profile. A processor outage fails transactions, so its risk is operational. But the processor is not the party that pays when a merchant's chargebacks exceed its reserves.
The lines blur because vendors span layers: many gateways also process, and many processors sell a gateway. A practical test works regardless of branding: if a provider can fail your transaction but cannot be held financially liable, it sits at the gateway or processor layer.
The acquiring bank: where money and liability sit
The acquiring bank is the only layer the card schemes define. PCI SSC describes the acquirer as an entity the payment brand designates as an acquirer, bound by that brand's rules on merchant compliance. It signs the merchant agreement, assigns the merchant ID and category code, and settles funds to the merchant's account.
It also carries the liability. Visa's Acceptance Risk Standards make the acquirer responsible for overseeing its merchants and third-party agents, and for the losses they incur. Even payment facilitators, which onboard sub-merchants themselves, must partner with an acquirer that meets Visa's requirements. However many intermediaries sit in between, responsibility flows up to a licensed institution.
This is also where pricing is set. Interchange flows from the acquirer to the card issuer and, in the EU, is capped at 0.2% for consumer debit and 0.3% for consumer credit transactions. Scheme fees pass through on top. The negotiable part is the acquirer's margin and its appetite for your risk profile. When a merchant says it negotiated better processing fees, it almost always negotiated with an acquiring bank.
That makes the acquirer the one layer you cannot abstract away. You can only add more acquirers, and that's where most payment stacks start to strain.
Payment orchestration vs payment gateway: the layer above the stack
Payment orchestration vs payment gateway is the comparison I see confused most often, partly because both present to the merchant as a single API. The difference lies in where decisions are made.
A gateway connects a checkout to one processing path, or to a few paths its owner has chosen. An orchestration layer sits above gateways, processors, and acquiring banks, and connects to many of them on the merchant's terms.
In practice, that means it:
decides which provider handles each transaction, based on market, currency, card type, cost, or recent approval rates;
retries soft declines through an alternative route instead of returning a failure to the customer;
normalizes response codes, fees, and settlement data from different providers into one format;
tokenizes card data at its own layer, so stored credentials are not tied to a single provider.
What orchestration does not do matters as much. It holds no acquiring license, takes on no chargeback liability, and replaces none of the merchant agreements you hold with acquiring banks. It works on top of those contracts. We built Corefy on that premise: the merchant keeps its direct provider relationships, and the orchestration layer gives its payment team control over how they are used.
The need for that control shows in the data. In our payment maturity study of 672 businesses, 58.5% operate at a fragmented stage, running several providers through separate dashboards, reports, and processes. Single-provider dependency fell to 33.5%, and the clearest maturity signal appears at five or more providers. Connecting providers has become easy. Running them as one system has not.
The strongest objection deserves a straight answer. Orchestration adds a layer, an integration, and a vendor. For a merchant in one market with one acquirer and stable approval rates, that cost is hard to justify, and I would tell them so. The calculation changes when a second acquirer arrives, whether for redundancy, local acquiring in a new market, or a better rate. From there, payment routing, reconciliation, and provider comparison become work someone has to do. The only choice is whether it lives in custom code and spreadsheets or in infrastructure built for it.
Mapping your own stack: five questions per provider
Most payment teams know their providers by brand name. Fewer know which layer each one actually occupies. Run every provider contract through these five questions:
Whose name is on the merchant agreement? That entity is your acquirer of record, regardless of what the provider calls itself.
Which fees are pass-through and which are margin? An interchange++ breakdown shows where your cost sits; a blended rate hides it.
Who holds your stored card tokens, and can you export them? If migrating customers' cards needs the provider's cooperation, your switching cost is higher than the contract suggests.
If approval rates fall in one market, which layer would you change? If the honest answer is 'all of them, because they come as a bundle', the bundle is limiting you.
Where does your reconciliation data come from? If each provider sends settlement reports in its own format, someone on your team is doing an orchestrator's job by hand.
Final thought
Gateways, processors, and acquiring banks are defined by what they own: data in transit, messages to the schemes, and money together with its liability. Orchestration owns none of these. It owns the decision about which of them handles each payment, and that decision now shapes approval rates, costs, and resilience more than any single provider contract does.
For payment leaders, the practical step is to know where each layer in your stack ends and who controls the boundaries between them. If the answer is 'our providers', it is worth revisiting.

title: Justin Sun Prize Partners With MathDB, Led by Caltech Professor Tony Yue Yu, on 50-Problem Pilot
summary: Geneva, Switzerland — October 26, 2026 — The Office of Justin Sun today announced a pilot program for the Justin Sun Prize in collaboration with MathDB, a mathematical research platform developed by Caltech Professor Tony Yue Yu and his team.    The Justin Sun Prize was established to become the “Nobel Prize of the AI Era,” responding to the profound transformation of scientific research and incentives in the new era in a more decentralized, formalized and machine-driven way. Problem-level awards can reach $1 million, subject to the applicable award terms and eligibility requirements.    The collaboration introduces a submission and review process through MathDB. MathDB will accept solution submissions, verify Lean formalizations and review expository materials, while the Justin Sun Prize will separately assess eligibility, attribution, priority and applicable award terms.   “AI is changing the speed at which mathematics can be explored, but speed alone is not scientific progress,” said Justin Sun, founder of the Justin Sun Prize. “The opportunity is to create a framework where human insight and machine intelligence can work together without compromising rigor. Working with MathDB brings mathematical discovery and machine-verifiable proof into the same process, which we believe can help define a more rigorous model for future discoveries.”   The pilot covers 50 problems across four award levels, with problem-level prize pools up to $1 million, depending on the problem. The highest tier includes P versus NP, the Riemann Hypothesis, Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap, the Hodge Conjecture, Global Langlands functoriality and the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture, among others. The full list of participating problems and applicable award terms will be available through MathDB and the Justin Sun Prize.   All awards are subject to full eligibility verification, compliance with anti-money laundering (AML/sanctions) laws, and official program rules available at https://www.hejustinsun.com/prize.   To broaden the reach and impact of advanced research, the MathDB pilot program will reward not only solutions to mathematical problems but also engaging and accessible communication of those solutions. The reward is divided into three categories: 50% for the mathematical solution, 30% for Lean formalization and 20% for qualifying exposition.   MathDB is a large-scale community database of mathematical definitions, theorems, conjectures and open problems, with the aim of making mathematical knowledge easier to organize, connect and build upon. The project incorporates Lean formalization and automated proof-verification capability alongside mathematical explanations and supporting research materials. Professor Tony Yue Yu from California Institute of Technology, together with his team, will be leading the scientific aspects of the pilot.   “Solving a fundamental math problem often leads to much more than an answer to the original question,” said Yu. “The process can reveal unexpected connections, introduce powerful tools and open entirely new directions of research. These developments can have an influence that extends across generations and disciplines. The Justin Sun Prize celebrates this spirit of exploration by drawing attention to challenging problems, supporting researchers who pursue them, and encouraging public dissemination of knowledge. Our collaboration with the Justin Sun Prize is grounded in the belief that pursuing fundamental research through decentralized, rigorous and verifiable approaches can accelerate the pace of discovery and scientific progress, and contribute to the advancement of human civilization.”   The full list of participating problems, submission requirements and review procedures will be available through MathDB (https://mathdb.com/) and the Justin Sun Prize (https://www.hejustinsun.com/prize).   About the Office of Justin Sun The Office of Justin Sun supports Justin Sun’s global business, philanthropic and public initiatives across technology, blockchain, artificial intelligence, scientific research, investment, art and space exploration.    Justin Sun is the Ambassador and former Permanent Representative of Grenada to the World Trade Organization and the Founder of TRON. TRON is the leading blockchain for the stablecoin revolution, processing over $13 trillion in volume since its inception. In the world’s emerging markets, people rely on USDT on TRON to access the global financial system.   A protégé of Alibaba founder Jack Ma, Sun has been recognized internationally for his work in the digital asset industry, including a Forbes cover profile in April 2025 and multiple appearances on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list. In August 2025, he flew aboard Blue Origin’s NS-34 mission, becoming the 712th person in history to travel to space. His broader interests span technology, investment, philanthropy, art, gaming, and space exploration.   Office of Justin Sun Contact: info@hejustinsun.com    About Justin Sun Prize  The Justin Sun Prize is an academic initiative established by Justin Sun to support advances in mathematics, formal verification, and AI-assisted scientific discovery. The prize is decentralized and built around the principle that mathematical work should be judged by the strength, rigor, and verifiability of the proof itself, not the prestige or reputation of those submitting it.   Justin Sun established the prize in his own name as a long-term commitment to return wealth created through mathematics and technology back to mathematics itself. Its legacy is intended to be defined by the body of work it recognizes and the laureates whose discoveries stand the test of time. The prize links clearly defined mathematical challenges to machine-verifiable proof. Its guiding principles are openness, public benefit and open-source access.   Visit https://www.hejustinsun.com/prize for more information.    Media Contact: media@hejustinsun.com

title: Whop Announces Funding Round at $5.1B Valuation, Led by Sequoia and Shopify Ventures
summary:
Whop, the technology company on a mission to deliver everyone a sustainable income, today announced a $200 million Series D at a $5.1 billion valuation, led by Sequoia and Shopify Ventures.
The new capital will accelerate Whop's global expansion and R&D efforts to make payment and advertising markets radically more efficient. This round marks Whop's second fundraise this year following an announcement of a $200 million strategic investment from Tether at a $1.6B valuation in February 2026.
Work is fundamentally changing and AI is calling traditional career paths into question. Entry level job opportunities are at an all time low. For a generation starting in a hole, Whop is a way for individuals to own their economic futures.
Whop's core customers are business operators, ranging from heads of product at high growth startups, to 16 year old first time entrepreneurs. Whop provides business operators with a gamified UI and extensive API, powering distribution, business creation, and money.
Roughly 25,000 business operators generate $550M on Whop each month. Whop also delivers an income to more than 50,000 other people who provide value to the businesses every month.
"We take inspiration from the traditional economy in designing Whop, and because businesses are the primary conduit by which people earn money and create value, we focus on them as our primary customer," said Steven Schwartz, Co-founder and CEO of Whop.
Most businesses on Whop service hyper specific customer needs, rather than broad mass-market products. The internet has made it possible to reach customers in markets that were once too small or fragmented to build a business around. Businesses built natively on Whop include invoicing software for trucking companies, emergency tree removal services, private jet booking platforms, neobanks for dropshippers, and marketplaces supplying data to humanoid robotics companies.
"They're doing about a half billion revenue, business is doing great, and we're helping humanity create businesses for people who can't find a job", said Doug Leone, Partner at Sequoia Capital.
In the past three months, Whop has launched:
Business Blueprints, which lets new operators launch a ready-to-sell business in a few clicks. Over 21,000 businesses have been created via Blueprints since the product launched 6 weeks ago.
Whop CLI, which debuted in July, making Whop's API compatible with any AI agent and allowing operators to run their businesses via prompts. The Whop CLI and MCP connectors collectively receive over 350,000 calls per day with over 14,700 monthly active users.
Economic Intelligence, a decision engine trained on millions of transactions that recommends the highest-ROI next move for each business. To access Economic Intelligence, businesses give an extra percentage of the revenue earned from using the system.
Whop is headquartered in Palo Alto, California with offices in New York and is hiring across engineering, product, sales, and operations.

title: Google DeepMind study finds LLMs can’t reliably roll their own dice
summary:
The inability of LLMs to generate true randomness poses security risks, necessitating external random inputs for reliable AI decision-making.
The post Google DeepMind study finds LLMs can’t reliably roll their own dice appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: A new study by Google DeepMind reveals that large language models struggle to generate true randomness when attempting to roll virtual dice. This limitation in producing reliable random numbers creates potential security risks for artificial intelligence systems. Researchers emphasize that these models require external random inputs to ensure safe and dependable decision-making in various applications.
content_ta: Google DeepMind நடத்திய புதிய ஆய்வில், பெரிய மொழி மாதிரிகளால் (LLMs) தாங்களாகவே நம்பகமான முறையில் சீரற்ற தன்மையை (randomness) உருவாக்க முடியவில்லை என்பது தெரியவந்துள்ளது. முறையான சீரற்ற எண்களை உருவாக்க முடியாத இந்த குறைபாடு, செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு அமைப்புகளுக்கு பாதுகாப்பு அபாயங்களை ஏற்படுத்துகிறது. பாதுகாப்பான முடிவெடுப்பதற்கு இந்த அமைப்புகளுக்கு வெளிப்புற சீரற்ற உள்ளீடுகள் தேவைப்படுவதாக ஆராய்ச்சியாளர்கள் வலியுறுத்துகின்றனர்.
